::: {.why}
Forty-seven drill sittings produced a record of exactly which problems you are slow on, which is a better study plan than any book's table of contents.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Classify every problem you have got wrong or been slow on into categories, and rank the categories by count.
- State the two categories that account for most of your errors and plan this week around them.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Build the classification: go through the file from last night and tag each problem by type, such as conditional probability, expectation by conditioning, symmetry, martingale, random walk, order statistics, combinatorics, or arithmetic. Count by tag and sort.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Look for the pattern behind the counts rather than only the counts: errors usually cluster around a technique you avoid rather than a topic you do not know. Write one sentence on what the top category has in common, then design the six sessions of this week around it, weighting the two largest categories most heavily.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Set the measurement: your timed mixed-set score from the last eight sittings is the baseline, and the target for the end of week 51 is a specific number you write down today.
:::
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
A tagged and counted error log with the top two categories identified and this week's six sessions planned around them.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
What are your two weakest problem categories, and what do they have in common?
:::
